import colors from 'colors';
import { just } from '../../../src/utils/organization/just';
import type { CoderRunUiHandle } from '../../run-codex-prompts/ui/renderCoderRunUi';
import type { AgentRunOptions } from '../AgentRunOptions';
import { createAgentIgnoreMatcher } from './agentIgnorePatterns';
import { AgentMessageFailureTracker } from './AgentMessageFailureTracker';
import { handleAgentWatchError } from './handleAgentWatchError';
import { loadLocalAgentRunnerProjectSummaries } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/loadLocalAgentRunnerProjectSummaries';
import { MultipleAgentAutoPuller } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/MultipleAgentAutoPuller';
import { MultipleAgentGithubSynchronizer } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/MultipleAgentGithubSynchronizer';
import { MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter';
import { RunMultipleAgentMessageTaskScheduler } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/RunMultipleAgentMessageTaskScheduler';
import { formatProjectPath } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/formatProjectPath';
import type { LocalAgentRunnerWorkItem } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/LocalAgentRunnerWorkItem';
import { wait } from './runMultipleAgentMessages/wait';
import { validateAgentRunOptions } from './validateAgentRunOptions';
import { validateAgentWatchOptions } from './validateAgentWatchOptions';

/**
 * Delay between multi-agent watch iterations while all queues stay empty.
 */
const MULTI_AGENT_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000;

/**
 * Optional integrations for callers that supervise the multi-agent watcher as one service.
 */
export type RunMultipleAgentMessagesControls = {
    readonly shouldContinue?: () => boolean;
    readonly queuePollIntervalMs?: number;
    readonly watchErrorLogDirectoryPath?: string;
    readonly onUiInitialized?: (uiHandle: CoderRunUiHandle | undefined) => void;
};

/**
 * Watches all direct child agent repositories from the current directory in one shared session.
 */
export async function runMultipleAgentMessages(
    options: AgentRunOptions,
    controls: RunMultipleAgentMessagesControls = {},
): Promise<void> {
    validateAgentRunOptions(options);
    validateAgentWatchOptions('ptbk agent-folder run-multiple', options);

    const rootPath = options.projectPath ?? process.cwd();
    const shouldContinue = controls.shouldContinue || (() => just(true));
    const queuePollIntervalMs = controls.queuePollIntervalMs ?? MULTI_AGENT_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS;
    const watchErrorLogDirectoryPath = controls.watchErrorLogDirectoryPath || rootPath;
    const ignoreMatcher = createAgentIgnoreMatcher(options.ignorePatterns);
    const githubSynchronizer = new MultipleAgentGithubSynchronizer();
    const autoPuller = new MultipleAgentAutoPuller();
    const messageFailureTracker = new AgentMessageFailureTracker({
        maxMessageProcessingFailures: options.maxMessageProcessingFailures,
    });
    let lastObservedProjectCount = 0;
    let isWatchSessionInitialized = false;
    let uiPresenter: MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter | undefined;
    let taskScheduler: RunMultipleAgentMessageTaskScheduler | undefined;

    while (shouldContinue()) {
        try {
            if (!isWatchSessionInitialized) {
                uiPresenter = MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter.create(options, rootPath);
                taskScheduler = new RunMultipleAgentMessageTaskScheduler({
                    runOptions: options,
                    messageFailureTracker,
                    autoPuller,
                    uiPresenter,
                    watchErrorLogDirectoryPath,
                });
                isWatchSessionInitialized = true;
                controls.onUiInitialized?.(uiPresenter.uiHandle);

                if (!uiPresenter.uiHandle) {
                    console.info(colors.green('Watching direct child agent repositories for queued messages.'));
                }
            }

            const currentUiPresenter = uiPresenter!;
            const currentTaskScheduler = taskScheduler!;

            await githubSynchronizer.synchronizeIfNeeded({
                rootPath,
                runOptions: options,
                ignoreMatcher,
                uiPresenter: currentUiPresenter,
                lastObservedProjectCount,
            });

            let projectSummariesResult = await loadLocalAgentRunnerProjectSummaries(rootPath, {
                includeMessagePreviews: Boolean(currentUiPresenter.uiHandle),
                ignoreMatcher,
            });
            let projectSummaries = projectSummariesResult.projectSummaries;
            lastObservedProjectCount = projectSummaries.length;
            let ignoredAgentCount = projectSummariesResult.ignoredProjectCount + githubSynchronizer.ignoredAgentCount;
            const autoPullResult =
                currentTaskScheduler.activeMessageCount === 0
                    ? await autoPuller.pullIfNeeded({
                          rootPath,
                          runOptions: options,
                          uiPresenter: currentUiPresenter,
                          projectSummaries,
                          ignoredAgentCount,
                      })
                    : {
                          isAnyRepositoryPulled: false,
                          pulledProjectPaths: new Set<string>(),
                      };

            if (autoPullResult.isAnyRepositoryPulled) {
                projectSummariesResult = await loadLocalAgentRunnerProjectSummaries(rootPath, {
                    includeMessagePreviews: Boolean(currentUiPresenter.uiHandle),
                    ignoreMatcher,
                });
                projectSummaries = projectSummariesResult.projectSummaries;
                lastObservedProjectCount = projectSummaries.length;
                ignoredAgentCount = projectSummariesResult.ignoredProjectCount + githubSynchronizer.ignoredAgentCount;
            }

            const queuedWorkItems = currentTaskScheduler.selectQueuedWorkItems(projectSummaries);
            const answeringProjectPaths = currentTaskScheduler.createAnsweringProjectPaths(queuedWorkItems);

            if (queuedWorkItems.length === 0 && currentTaskScheduler.activeMessageCount === 0) {
                currentUiPresenter.updateForWatching(projectSummaries, ignoredAgentCount);
                await wait(queuePollIntervalMs);
                continue;
            }

            if (queuedWorkItems.length === 0) {
                currentUiPresenter.updateForAnswering({
                    projectSummaries,
                    answeringProjectPaths,
                    ignoredAgentCount,
                    activeMessageCount: currentTaskScheduler.activeMessageCount,
                });
                await currentTaskScheduler.waitForNextTurn(queuePollIntervalMs);
                continue;
            }

            announceQueuedWorkItems(rootPath, currentUiPresenter, queuedWorkItems);
            currentUiPresenter.updateForAnswering({
                projectSummaries,
                answeringProjectPaths,
                ignoredAgentCount,
                activeMessageCount: currentTaskScheduler.activeMessageCount + queuedWorkItems.length,
            });
            currentTaskScheduler.startQueuedWorkItems({
                queuedWorkItems,
                projectSummaries,
                answeringProjectPaths,
                ignoredAgentCount,
                autoPullResult,
            });

            await currentTaskScheduler.waitForNextTurn(queuePollIntervalMs);
        } catch (error) {
            await handleAgentWatchError({
                commandDisplayName: 'ptbk agent-folder run-multiple',
                logDirectoryPath: watchErrorLogDirectoryPath,
                error,
            });
            await messageFailureTracker.recordFailure(error);
            await wait(queuePollIntervalMs);
        }
    }

    await taskScheduler?.waitForActiveTasksToSettle();
}

/**
 * Prints queued work in legacy no-UI mode.
 *
 * @private function of `runMultipleAgentMessages`
 */
function announceQueuedWorkItems(
    rootPath: string,
    uiPresenter: MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter,
    queuedWorkItems: ReadonlyArray<LocalAgentRunnerWorkItem>,
): void {
    if (uiPresenter.uiHandle) {
        return;
    }

    for (const queuedWorkItem of queuedWorkItems) {
        console.info(
            colors.blue(
                `Processing ${formatProjectPath(rootPath, queuedWorkItem.projectSummary.project.projectPath)}/${
                    queuedWorkItem.queuedMessage.relativePath
                } with ${queuedWorkItem.projectSummary.localAgentName}.`,
            ),
        );
    }
}

import colors from 'colors';
import type { AgentRunOptions } from '../../AgentRunOptions';
import type { AgentIgnoreMatcher } from '../agentIgnorePatterns';
import { shouldRunPeriodicTask } from '../shouldRunPeriodicTask';
import { synchronizeGithubAgentRunnerRepositories } from '../synchronizeGithubAgentRunnerRepositories';
import type { MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter } from './MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter';

/**
 * Delay between GitHub owner synchronization rounds while the multi-agent runner stays active.
 */
const MULTI_AGENT_GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;

/**
 * Delay between GitHub owner synchronization rounds while no local repositories exist yet.
 */
const MULTI_AGENT_EMPTY_DIRECTORY_GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000;

/**
 * Owns periodic GitHub repository synchronization state for `runMultipleAgentMessages`.
 *
 * @private class of `runMultipleAgentMessages`
 */
export class MultipleAgentGithubSynchronizer {
    private synchronizationTimestamp: number | undefined;
    private ignoredRepositoryCount = 0;

    /**
     * Number of remote repositories ignored during the last synchronization round.
     */
    public get ignoredAgentCount(): number {
        return this.ignoredRepositoryCount;
    }

    /**
     * Synchronizes missing local repositories from GitHub when the owner configuration is available.
     */
    public async synchronizeIfNeeded(options: {
        readonly rootPath: string;
        readonly runOptions: AgentRunOptions;
        readonly ignoreMatcher: AgentIgnoreMatcher;
        readonly uiPresenter: MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter;
        readonly lastObservedProjectCount: number;
    }): Promise<void> {
        const { rootPath, runOptions, ignoreMatcher, uiPresenter, lastObservedProjectCount } = options;

        if (!runOptions.autoClone) {
            this.ignoredRepositoryCount = 0;
            return;
        }

        const synchronizationIntervalMs =
            lastObservedProjectCount === 0
                ? MULTI_AGENT_EMPTY_DIRECTORY_GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS
                : MULTI_AGENT_GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS;

        if (
            !shouldRunPeriodicTask({
                lastRunTimestamp: this.synchronizationTimestamp,
                intervalMs: synchronizationIntervalMs,
            })
        ) {
            return;
        }

        uiPresenter.updateForGithubSynchronization(lastObservedProjectCount);

        const synchronizationResult = await synchronizeGithubAgentRunnerRepositories(rootPath, { ignoreMatcher });
        this.ignoredRepositoryCount = synchronizationResult.ignoredRepositoryNames?.length || 0;

        if (!uiPresenter.uiHandle && synchronizationResult.clonedRepositoryNames.length > 0) {
            console.info(
                colors.gray(
                    `Cloned ${synchronizationResult.clonedRepositoryNames.length} new agent repositor${
                        synchronizationResult.clonedRepositoryNames.length === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'
                    }: ${synchronizationResult.clonedRepositoryNames.join(', ')}`,
                ),
            );
        }

        this.synchronizationTimestamp = synchronizationResult.synchronizedAt ?? this.synchronizationTimestamp;
    }
}
/**
 * Waits for the next idle poll interval in multi-agent watch mode.
 *
 * @private function of `runMultipleAgentMessages`
 */
export async function wait(delayMs: number): Promise<void> {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
}
import colors from 'colors';
import type { AgentRunOptions } from '../../AgentRunOptions';
import { pullLatestChangesForAgentQueueIfEnabled } from '../pullLatestChangesForAgentQueueIfEnabled';
import { shouldRunPeriodicTask } from '../shouldRunPeriodicTask';
import { formatProjectPath } from './formatProjectPath';
import type { LocalAgentRunnerProjectSummary } from './LocalAgentRunnerProjectSummary';
import type { MultiAgentAutoPullResult } from './MultiAgentAutoPullResult';
import type { MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter } from './MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter';

/**
 * Delay between idle auto-pull rounds for each watched child repository.
 */
const MULTI_AGENT_IDLE_AUTO_PULL_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;

/**
 * Owns periodic auto-pull state for watched local repositories.
 *
 * @private class of `runMultipleAgentMessages`
 */
export class MultipleAgentAutoPuller {
    private readonly autoPullTimestampsByProjectPath = new Map<string, number>();

    /**
     * Pulls latest changes for watched child repositories when their idle auto-pull interval elapsed.
     */
    public async pullIfNeeded(options: {
        readonly rootPath: string;
        readonly runOptions: AgentRunOptions;
        readonly uiPresenter: MultipleAgentRunUiPresenter;
        readonly projectSummaries: ReadonlyArray<LocalAgentRunnerProjectSummary>;
        readonly ignoredAgentCount: number;
    }): Promise<MultiAgentAutoPullResult> {
        const { rootPath, runOptions, uiPresenter, projectSummaries, ignoredAgentCount } = options;
        const pulledProjectPaths = new Set<string>();

        if (!runOptions.autoPull || projectSummaries.length === 0) {
            return { isAnyRepositoryPulled: false, pulledProjectPaths };
        }

        this.pruneTimestampsForCurrentProjects(projectSummaries);

        const projectSummariesToPull = projectSummaries.filter((projectSummary) =>
            shouldRunPeriodicTask({
                lastRunTimestamp: this.autoPullTimestampsByProjectPath.get(projectSummary.project.projectPath),
                intervalMs: MULTI_AGENT_IDLE_AUTO_PULL_INTERVAL_MS,
            }),
        );

        if (projectSummariesToPull.length === 0) {
            return { isAnyRepositoryPulled: false, pulledProjectPaths };
        }

        if (uiPresenter.uiHandle) {
            uiPresenter.updateForAutoPull(projectSummaries, ignoredAgentCount, projectSummariesToPull);
        } else {
            console.info(
                colors.gray(
                    `Pulling latest changes for ${projectSummariesToPull.length} watched agent repositor${
                        projectSummariesToPull.length === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'
                    }...`,
                ),
            );
        }

        for (const projectSummary of projectSummariesToPull) {
            const projectPath = projectSummary.project.projectPath;
            const autoPullTimestamp = await pullLatestChangesForAgentQueueIfEnabled({
                projectPath,
                runOptions,
                logMessage: uiPresenter.uiHandle
                    ? undefined
                    : `Pulling latest changes in ${formatProjectPath(rootPath, projectPath)}...`,
            });

            if (autoPullTimestamp !== undefined) {
                this.recordAutoPullTimestamp(projectPath, autoPullTimestamp);
                pulledProjectPaths.add(projectPath);
            }
        }

        return {
            isAnyRepositoryPulled: pulledProjectPaths.size > 0,
            pulledProjectPaths,
        };
    }

    /**
     * Records an auto-pull timestamp observed while a child runner processed one message.
     */
    public recordAutoPullTimestamp(projectPath: string, autoPullTimestamp: number): void {
        this.autoPullTimestampsByProjectPath.set(projectPath, autoPullTimestamp);
    }

    private pruneTimestampsForCurrentProjects(projectSummaries: ReadonlyArray<LocalAgentRunnerProjectSummary>): void {
        const currentProjectPaths = new Set(
            projectSummaries.map((projectSummary) => projectSummary.project.projectPath),
        );

        for (const projectPath of this.autoPullTimestampsByProjectPath.keys()) {
            if (!currentProjectPaths.has(projectPath)) {
                this.autoPullTimestampsByProjectPath.delete(projectPath);
            }
        }
    }
}

        const loopStates = [true, false];
        await runMultipleAgentMessages(createAgentRunOptions(), {
            shouldContinue: () => loopStates.shift() ?? false,
        });

        expect(tickAgentMessages).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
        const errorLogFileName = (await readdir(temporaryRootDirectory)).find((fileName) =>
            /^ptbk-agent-error-.*\.log$/u.test(fileName),
        );

        expect(errorLogFileName).toBeDefined();
        expect(await readFile(join(temporaryRootDirectory, errorLogFileName!), 'utf-8')).toContain(
            'echo failing agent',
        );
        expect(consoleErrorSpy).toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('moves a repeatedly failing child message to failed after the configured retry cap', async () => {
        temporaryRootDirectory = await createTemporaryRootDirectory();
        const agentProjectPath = join(temporaryRootDirectory, 'agent-a');
        await mkdir(join(agentProjectPath, 'messages', 'queued'), { recursive: true });
        await writeFile(join(agentProjectPath, 'agent.book'), 'Agent A', 'utf-8');
        await writeFile(join(agentProjectPath, 'messages', 'queued', 'question.book'), 'MESSAGE @User\nA\n', 'utf-8');

        (tickAgentMessages as jest.MockedFunction<typeof tickAgentMessages>).mockImplementation(
            async (_options, tickOptions) => {
                throw withAgentWatchErrorContext(new Error('No authentication information found.'), {
                    projectPath: tickOptions?.projectPath,
                    queuedMessageRelativePath: 'messages/queued/question.book',
                });
            },
        );

        process.chdir(temporaryRootDirectory);

        const loopStates = [true, true, false];
        await runMultipleAgentMessages(createAgentRunOptions({ maxMessageProcessingFailures: 2 }), {
            shouldContinue: () => loopStates.shift() ?? false,
        });

        expect(tickAgentMessages).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
        expect(await readdir(join(agentProjectPath, 'messages', 'queued'))).toEqual([]);
        const failedMessage = await readFile(join(agentProjectPath, 'messages', 'failed', 'question.book'), 'utf-8');
        expect(failedMessage).toContain('Local agent runner failed after 2 attempt(s) and stopped retrying.');
        expect(failedMessage).toContain('No authentication information found.');
    });
});

/**
 * Returns true when one periodic background task should run now.
 */
export function shouldRunPeriodicTask(options: {
    readonly lastRunTimestamp: number | undefined;
    readonly intervalMs: number;
}): boolean {
    const { lastRunTimestamp, intervalMs } = options;

    if (lastRunTimestamp === undefined) {
        return true;
    }

    return Date.now() - lastRunTimestamp >= intervalMs;
}

'use strict';

const { spawn } = require('node:child_process');
const path = require('node:path');

/**
 * Absolute repository root used as the default working directory for verification steps.
 */
const PROJECT_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');

/**
 * Agents Server workspace used by the final lint/build verification steps.
 */
const AGENTS_SERVER_ROOT = path.join(PROJECT_ROOT, 'apps', 'agents-server');

/**
 * Platform-specific npm executable name.
 */
const NPM_COMMAND = 'npm';

/**
 * Ordered verification steps for `npm run test-for-ptbk-coder`.
 */
const TEST_FOR_PTBK_CODER_STEPS = [
    { script: 'test-name-discrepancies', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-spellcheck', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-lint', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-types', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-books', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-book-components-build', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-package-generation', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-unit', cwd: PROJECT_ROOT },
    { script: 'lint', cwd: AGENTS_SERVER_ROOT },
    { script: 'test-build', cwd: AGENTS_SERVER_ROOT },
];

/**
 * Runs one npm script and resolves only after the child process and its stdio streams are fully closed.
 *
 * @param {{script: string, cwd: string}} step - Verification step definition.
 * @returns {Promise<void>} Promise that resolves on success.
 */
function runVerificationStep(step) {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const childProcess = spawn(`${NPM_COMMAND} run ${step.script}`, {
            cwd: step.cwd,
            stdio: 'inherit',
            env: process.env,
            shell: true,
        });

        childProcess.on('error', (error) => {
            reject(error);
        });

        childProcess.on('close', (code, signal) => {
            if (code === 0) {
                resolve();
                return;
            }

            reject(
                new Error(
                    `Verification step \`${step.script}\` failed with code ${String(code)} and signal ${String(signal)}.`,
                ),
            );
        });
    });
}

/**
 * Executes the Promptbook Coder verification suite from the lightest checks to the heaviest build step.
 */
async function main() {
    console.info('Note: Running from most lightweight to heaviest tests');

    for (const step of TEST_FOR_PTBK_CODER_STEPS) {
        await runVerificationStep(step);
    }

    console.info('🎉 All tests passed!');
}

void main().catch((error) => {
    console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});

./changelog/_current-preversion.md:1175:-   Fixed `\`headers\` was called outside a request scope`crash during the standalone VPS Agents Server installation. The bundled-default-agents step runs the`seedDefaultAgents.ts`script via`tsx`outside any Next.js request, but`seedCoreAgents`reached for table names through`$getTableName('Agent')` / `$getTableName('AgentFolder')`, which transitively called `$provideServer()` → `next/headers#headers()` and threw on the bare CLI. The two internal helpers (`loadExistingActiveAgentNames` and `ensureCoreFolderExists`) now accept the `tablePrefix` already resolved by `seedCoreAgents` from `options.tablePrefix ?? process.env.SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX ?? ''` and build the prefixed `Agent` / `AgentFolder` table names directly, mirroring the synchronous concatenation pattern used by `AgentCollectionInSupabase.getTableName`. The Next.js-request-scoped `$getTableName`import is dropped from`seedCoreAgents.ts`, so the standalone seeder no longer touches request-scope APIs — request-handling code paths keep using `$getTableName`unchanged. The companion`registerServerErrorSentryLogging.test.ts`"keeps logging locally when Sentry is not configured" case is also tightened to clear`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`along with`SENTRY_DSN`(and to restore it in`afterEach`), because `resolveOptionalSentryDsn`falls back to the public DSN — the previous test passed only on machines without a populated`.env`, and the local `npm run test-for-ptbk-coder` verification surfaced it.

Commitments are applied one by one, so a\n    commitment used several times in one book emitted its whole section every time, including the shared guidance\n    paragraph which introduces it. Two `WRITING RULES` blocks produced two `## Writing rules` headings each preceded by\n    the same four-line explanation of what a writing rule is, two `USE PRIVACY` blocks produced the `## Privacy`\n    instructions twice, and the same held for `WRITING SAMPLE`, `SAMPLE`, `LANGUAGE`, `USE POPUP`,\n    `USE IMAGE GENERATOR`, `USE USER LOCATION` and `TEAM`. The final system message is now deduplicated once for all\n    commitments instead of being fixed in each of them separately:\n\n    -   All sections sharing one `## Title` are merged into the position of their first occurrence, so each heading\n        appears exactly once while the content of every commitment keeps its original order inside that section.\n    -   Every identical block is kept only once, so the shared guidance paragraph of a repeated commitment is stated\n        once and a repeated instruction without its own heading, such as `STYLE Formal.` written twice, is no longer\n        duplicated.\n    -   Merged bullet lists stay one compact list, and fenced code blocks - imported files and inline `KNOWLEDGE`\n        content among them - are never split or deduplicated.\n    -   Commitments written once produce exactly the same system message as before.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and","originalFile":"-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and\n    thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now\n    names the agent which implemented it:\n\n    -   A prompt status line signs its work with the agent in front of the harness, as\n        `` [x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.13 23 minutes ``.\n        The `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status lines and the run trace of the round all report it, and a prompt continued\n        through `--git-changes continue` keeps the agent in each of its chronological `interrupted, continued by …`\n        reports.\n    -   The reported name is the display name of the Book — its `META FULLNAME`, or the plain title on its first line\n        — so `agents/coding/developer.book` signs as its Book title and not as its normalized identifier.\n    -   A run started without `--agent` reports exactly what it reported before.\n\n-   Fixed `MockedChat` typing animations blinking for messages without ids by assigning stable playback-only ids before rendering each simulated transcript.\n\n-   Fixed the rich `ptbk coder run` dashboard so an animated agent avatar can no longer overwrite its own UI in an\n    exact-width terminal pane:\n\n    -   The shared frame layout now leaves one physical terminal column unused, preventing boxed rows from\n        auto-wrapping and keeping incremental cursor-based redraws aligned with their logical frame rows.\n    -   Added a focused VS Code terminal preset and regression coverage for the terminal-width invariant.\n\n-   Added agent-specific prompt routing to `ptbk coder`:\n\n    -   A ready `[ ]` prompt can now target the Book passed in `--agent` with a backtick-delimited path, filename,\n        filename without `.book`, or the Book title from its first line. For example, a run using\n        `--agent agents/coding/developer.book` accepts `agents/coding/developer.book`, `developer.book`,\n        `developer`, and `Promptbook Developer` routing tokens.\n    -   Agent references work alongside the existing model and harness routing tokens, and `ptbk coder list --agent\n        <path.book>` previews the same agent-specific queue without starting a harness.\n    -   Added an Unslopper agent preset next to the developer preset in the local VS Code terminal scripts and\n        documented agent-specific routing on the `ptbk coder` landing page.\n\n-   The help of `ptbk` does not advertise the deprecated commands anymore. `run`, `login`, `make`, `prettify`, `test`,\n    `list-models`, `list-scrapers`, `start-agents-server` and `start-pipelines-server` are all leftovers of the old\n    pipeline system, yet nine of the fifteen commands which `ptbk --help` listed were exactly those, each one with its\n    own `Deprecated:` paragraph, so the listing which is supposed to introduce the CLI was mostly made of commands\n    nobody should start using. `ptbk --help`, and the same listing which plain `ptbk` prints when it asks for a\n    subcommand, now offers only the commands which are meant to be used - `coder`, `agent`, `agent-folder`,\n    `agents-server`, `about` and `hello`. Nothing was removed: every deprecated command still runs, still warns that it\n    is deprecated when it is used, still explains the deprecation in its own help - `ptbk run --help` - and is still\n    reachable through `ptbk help run`. Only the \"did you mean\" hint for a mistyped command stops pointing at them.\n    Being left out of the help is now simply a part of what deprecating a command means, written once in\n    `$deprecateCliCommand`, so any command deprecated later disappears from the help on its own.\n\n-   `ptbk` without a subcommand no longer falls back to the deprecated `ptbk run`. Until now `run` was registered as\n    the default command of the CLI, so everything which did not name a command - `ptbk ./write-cv.book`, a mistyped\n    `ptbk codr` or a stray option - was quietly handed over to the pipeline runner of the old system, which was the\n    last thing a deprecated command should be doing. Plain `ptbk` now asks to specify a subcommand and prints the\n    top-level help, exactly like `ptbk coder`, `ptbk agent`, `ptbk agent-folder` and `ptbk agents-server` already did\n    when they were called without one of their own subcommands, and that one shared behavior is now written once\n    instead of five times. Anything which is not a command is refused with `unknown command` and a \"did you mean\"\n    hint instead of being executed as a pipeline, so a script which still passes a book path to `ptbk` fails loudly\n    rather than appearing to succeed. `ptbk run` itself is untouched and keeps working for everyone who asks for it\n    explicitly. The command list in the help now starts with `coder`, followed by `agent`, `agent-folder` and\n    `agents-server`, and the deprecated commands of the old pipeline system are listed after them.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now saves the run trace of every prompt round, so a finished run can still be analyzed afterwards.\n    Until now the only durable record of a round was the one status line written into the prompt file: the live\n    runtime log holding everything the harness and the verification command had written was a temporary artifact,\n    deleted as soon as a successful round was over unless `--preserve-logs` was passed, and lost together with the\n    reasoning, the tool calls and the diffs of the run. Each round now writes `prompts/traces/<prompt-file-name>.md`\n    - a trace named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to, with the same `-2` section suffix the temporary\n    scripts of a multi-section prompt file already use. The trace pairs the metadata of the round - which prompt and\n    section it implemented, whether it succeeded or failed, the harness, model, thinking level and login method which\n    ran it, how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran, the verification\n    command, the start, end and duration, and the error which ended a failed round - with the untouched runtime log\n    of the harness. Because the trace is written before the round is committed, it lands in the very same commit as\n    the prompt it describes, and a task whose isolated worktree cannot be merged back carries its trace into the\n    failure commit instead. A failed round is traced too, next to the `.error.log` it already wrote. Re-running the\n    same prompt overwrites its trace and leaves the earlier ones in the git history.\n\n-   `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server` no longer walk into a full disk. A coding round writes prompt and log\n    artifacts, lets the harness rewrite the project, may install npm packages, may create a git worktree for\n    `--isolate` and usually runs a build, so a run started without enough space used to die somewhere in the middle,\n    after the coding agent had already rewritten a part of the project. The free disk space is now measured before\n    anything is installed or written: with less than 2 GB left the command refuses to start and says how much space\n    is left, how much is needed and how to get it back, instead of failing later with a raw filesystem error. The\n    same measurement is repeated while the run is in progress - at the checkpoints where `ptbk coder` can stop\n    anyway, so it is checked before every round, every verification and every commit - and once less than 1 GB is\n    left the run reports the same warning and pauses there, waiting for the disk space to be freed and for `P` to\n    resume it. The limit to keep running is lower than the limit to start, because interrupting a round which is\n    already in progress costs more than not starting one. A run started with `--no-questions` never pauses, because\n    there is nobody who could free the disk space and resume it - it reports the warning and keeps going. A platform\n    which cannot report its free disk space never stops a run.\n\n-   Added `--no-questions` to every `ptbk coder` command which can stop and wait for an answer it does not strictly\n    need. `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server` still do all their work, but no longer ask anything: installing\n    a missing coding harness, updating an outdated one, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing\n    harness ignore rules to `.gitignore` are all skipped and reported together with the command which does them\n    manually, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it. Because an outdated\n    harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, `--no-questions` also skips the npm latest-version\n    lookup which would only lead to a question, which is what the never released `--no-harness-update` used to do -\n    that flag is replaced by `--no-questions` and is gone. The one combination which can not work,\n    `--no-auto --no-questions`, is refused right away instead of waiting forever for a confirmation nobody may be\n    asked for. `ptbk coder verify` does not take the flag, because walking through finished prompts and asking about\n    each of them is the only thing it does.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` no longer answers a harness which is not logged in with a wall of raw CLI output. A harness whose\n    login is missing or whose session has expired now fails with a short branded `AuthenticationError` which names\n    the harness, quotes the one sentence the harness itself reported - such as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session\n    expired and could not be refreshed` - and says exactly how to sign in again, for example by running `claude` and\n    then the `/login` command inside it. How each harness is signed in is described once, next to how it is installed\n    and detected, and the failure is recognized once for every harness and for every command\n    which runs prompts, so `coder run`, `coder server` and `coder ping` all report it the same way. The terminal and\n    the `.error.log` file written next to the prompt both show those instructions on their own now, instead of\n    following them with a stack trace of a failure nobody can debug. Because no retry of a harness which is not\n    logged in can ever succeed, such a prompt is also no longer retried three times with the `--wait-after-error`\n    delay in between - the instructions are shown right away.\n\n-   Fixed the wall of `npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings printed when installing `ptbk`:\n\n    -   The Vercel AI SDK providers `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google` and `@ai-sdk/deepseek` were still on the\n        generation which accepts only Zod 3, while the rest of the ecosystem - the Agents Server, `@openai/agents`,\n        `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` - needs Zod 4. No single Zod could satisfy both sides, so npm reported a conflict\n        for every one of those packages. They are upgraded to the newest generation which accepts both Zod 3 and\n        Zod 4 and still runs on Node.js 18, so the supported Node.js versions of Promptbook do not change, and\n        `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` is migrated to the model interface of that generation. Settings\n        given as `additionalChatSettings` are now passed to the model call instead of to the model constructor,\n        which is where the Vercel AI SDK expects them, and the `userId` option is no longer sent as the `user`\n        setting, because it has become specific to each provider.\n    -   Generated packages no longer publish dependencies which only look like imports. Package generation infers\n        dependencies by reading the generated bundle, and it used to count module specifiers written inside the\n        source-code templates of the transpilers, so `@promptbook/core` published `zod`, `dotenv` and\n        `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as runtime dependencies although it never imports any of them. The pinned `zod` in\n        particular forced one exact Zod version onto every project which installs Promptbook.\n    -   Generated packages no longer carry the `overrides` field of the repository. npm honors overrides only in the\n        root project of an installation, so publishing them only left a dangling reference to a dependency which the\n        published package does not declare.\n\n    What remains after this are three warnings about React 19 coming from packages inside `swagger-ui-react`, which\n    are declared by projects outside of Promptbook.\n\n-   The hero headline of the **ptbk coder** landing page now rotates through seven claims instead of saying one\n    thing forever. Every claim is written once in a single configuration the rotating headline, the page tagline\n    and the sharing image all read, and the claims crossfade with a slight vertical slide - the claim which leaves\n    rises out of the headline while the next one rises into it. All claims share one grid cell, so the headline\n    keeps the height of the tallest of them and nothing around it moves while they rotate. The same reserved\n    height finally balances the hero: together with a terminal text size tuned one step down, the copy column now\n    reaches almost as high as the live terminal next to it, instead of floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defines. Visitors whose system prefers reduced motion keep the first claim without rotation.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` overwriting configuration the project already owns. Existing `package.json` scripts and\n    `.vscode/settings.json` settings are now kept verbatim and only genuinely missing ones are added. Files a default\n    script points at, like `agents/developer.book`, `AGENTS.md` and `prompts/templates/common.md`, are created only\n    together with the script which references them, so a project with its own `coder:run` no longer receives an unused\n    default agent. `ptbk coder init` also initializes the `test-for-ptbk-coder` npm script which the default\n    `coder:run` uses as its verification command.\n\n-   Rebalanced the hero of the **ptbk coder** landing page, whose live terminal used to be much taller than the copy\n    next to it and left the headline, the install command and the buttons floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defined:\n\n    -   The terminal window is now never wider than the character grid it draws, so a layout with more width than the\n        widest supported terminal - a tablet, a phone in landscape - gets a centered window instead of a window with an\n        empty half, and it fills the height of the copy column whenever the copy is the taller one.\n    -   A terminal row is now as tight as a real terminal emulator draws it, which both shortens the sample session by\n        about one tenth and keeps the frames of the dashboard boxes connected.\n    -   The box drawing characters, the shade of the progress bar and the status marks are missing from the latin\n        subset of the terminal font, so they were drawn from the fallback which `next/font` derives from a\n        **proportional** font - about one and a half character cells wide and shorter than one row, which broke every\n        box border of the dashboard into detached segments. The terminal font now falls back to the monospace fonts of\n        the system, so those characters are drawn one cell wide and one row tall and the boxes are drawn as continuous\n        frames.\n    -   The hero copy is now read at hero size: the headline and the subheadline grow with the viewport, but only as\n        far as their own column can carry them, so the headline keeps its two lines from the narrowest phone to the\n        widest desktop.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` so it no longer creates an `AGENT_CODING.md` quick-reference file.\n-   Redesigned the three core benefit illustrations on the **ptbk coder** landing page with detailed terminal,\n    portable-agent, and synchronized-commit scenes, plus proportional graphics and a more readable tablet layout.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` to preserve a non-empty `prompts/` directory instead of adding placeholder boilerplate\n    prompts while it initializes the remaining coder files.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder list`, a read-only queue preview that lists ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority\n    groups without starting a harness. Its optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and\n    `--max-priority` filters let you preview exactly the queue a selected runner would receive.\n\n-   Added a live GitHub star counter and **Star on GitHub** call to action to the **ptbk coder** landing page.\n\n-   Added support for plain markdown prompts without a status checkbox in **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder run` and\n    `ptbk coder server` now treat them as ready prompts at priority `0`, then insert the normal live `[^]` status line\n    before their content as processing begins and finish them through the usual `[x]` or `[!]` flow.\n\n-   Added queue opt-out markers to **ptbk coder**. `[.]` now behaves like `[-]`, keeping that prompt out of the queue,\n    and `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown prompt file excludes the entire file from `run`, `list`, and\n    `server`.\n\n-   Added project-local harness ignore rules to **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder init` now adds the rules for every supported\n    harness, including `.qwen`; `ptbk coder run`, `ptbk coder server`, and `ptbk coder ping` detect a missing selected\n    harness rule and use the same interactive `[y/N]` confirmation as harness installation updates before adding it.\n\n-   Fixed globally installing `ptbk` on Node.js 26, including macOS arm64. `ptbk coder` can now be installed without\n    `better-sqlite3` 11 falling back to a native build against removed V8 APIs; the generated CLI now receives\n    `better-sqlite3` 12.11.1, which supplies the matching Node 26 binary.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server production build failing when its Edge middleware reached standalone SQLite code.\n    SQLite registry loading now lives in a Node.js-only module, and custom-domain routing reads its needed federation\n    settings through the middleware's supplied Supabase client. Edge middleware can therefore route configured domains\n    without compiling `better-sqlite3` into its bundle.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder --harness openai-codex --model default` failing for everyone signed in to OpenAI Codex with a\n    ChatGPT account. `default` silently stood for `gpt-5.2-codex`, which such an account rejects with\n    _\"The 'gpt-5.2-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account\"_ — so both\n    `ptbk coder ping` and `ptbk coder run` died before doing any work.\n\n    -   `--model default` now overrides **no model at all** for OpenAI Codex: Codex is started without `--model` and\n        keeps the model from its own configuration _(`~/.codex/config.toml`)_, exactly like `--model default` already\n        worked for GitHub Copilot. Whatever a ChatGPT-account login is allowed to use therefore works.\n    -   Naming a model explicitly, for example `--model gpt-5.2-codex`, is unchanged, and `--model` is still required\n        for OpenAI Codex.\n    -   For `gemini` and `qwen-code`, `default` keeps standing for their concrete default model, because those CLIs\n        have no configured default to fall back to.\n    -   When Codex picks the model itself, the reported price is estimated from the fallback pricing, because only\n        Codex knows which model it really used.\n\n-   Fixed **ptbk coder** updating a coding harness with `npm install -g` even when npm does not own that harness. A\n    Codex installed by the official standalone installer was reported as outdated and \"updated\" into a _second_ Codex\n    inside the active Node prefix, while the Codex which actually runs stayed on its old version — and which of the two\n    was used from then on depended on the active Node version.\n\n    -   Before offering an update, `ptbk coder` now resolves which file the harness command really executes _(following\n        symbolic links, using the very same `PATH` which runs the harness)_ and recognizes whether it belongs to a\n        global npm installation, a standalone installation, or Homebrew.\n    -   A **standalone installation is updated with its own updater** — `codex update` for OpenAI Codex — and a\n        **Homebrew installation is never touched**, only `brew upgrade …` is printed. When the harness command cannot\n        be traced to any of these, `ptbk coder` says so and leaves it alone instead of guessing, because\n        `npm install -g` would install a second copy next to it.\n    -   The outdated-harness warning now also prints the resolved command path and how it was installed, and the\n        confirmation question names the exact command which is about to run, so an update can no longer be approved\n        without knowing what it does.\n    -   Installing a harness which is missing altogether is unchanged: it is still installed globally through npm.\n\n-   Added the singular `WRITING RULE` keyword as an equivalent variant of `WRITING RULES`, exactly like `RULE` and\n    `RULES` are interchangeable. Both spellings are parsed, applied, documented, and syntax-highlighted identically, so\n    a single writing constraint no longer has to be written in plural.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server starting one more pm2 process of the same agent project on every single start, which\n    eventually took the whole server down.\n\n    -   Every project runtime is registered under a stable pm2 process name, and a project was expected to be replaced\n        rather than duplicated because it is deleted right before it is started again. That delete was **skipped\n        whenever pm2 could not be asked for its process list**, and `pm2 start` appends a second process instead of\n        refusing a name it already knows, so each start added one more copy of the same project.\n    -   The process list could not be read because `pm2 jlist` embeds a full environment snapshot into every listed\n        process — roughly 70 kB each — while its output was capped at one megabyte. A dozen projects were enough to\n        exceed that cap, after which **every** pm2 query failed with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` and reported\n        every process as unknown. Each new duplicate made the output larger, so the failure never recovered on its own.\n    -   Every duplicate got its own port but the project's dev command kept binding the port it had chosen itself, so\n        all but one copy crash-looped on `EADDRINUSE`, and pm2 restarted them hundreds of times per hour until the VPS\n        ran out of threads (`pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable`) and the Agents Server itself was\n        killed.\n    -   Deleting a project process no longer depends on reading the process list: it is always attempted, only pm2\n        itself reporting an unknown name counts as \"already gone\", and any other failure is reported instead of\n        swallowed — so a project is now left alone rather than duplicated when pm2 misbehaves. Because `pm2 delete`\n        removes every process sharing one name, a server which already accumulated duplicates converges back to a\n        single process per project.\n\n-   Added the **Qwen Code** harness, so `ptbk coder` now drives seven coding agents instead of six.\n\n    -   `ptbk coder run --harness qwen-code --model qwen3.8-max` runs the whole prompt queue through the Qwen Code CLI,\n        and every other harness-aware command — `ptbk coder ping`, `ptbk coder server`, `ptbk agent exec`, `CliAgent`\n        and the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable — accepts `qwen-code` the same way.\n    -   Like `openai-codex` and `gemini`, Qwen Code **requires an explicit `--model`**; `--model default` resolves to\n        `qwen3.8-max`. Its global `@qwen-code/qwen-code` installation is checked and updated before the first prompt,\n        just like the other harnesses. Qwen Code exposes no reasoning-effort flag, so `--thinking-level` does not\n        apply to it.\n    -   Price estimation of harnesses which do not report their own token counts is now shared between Qwen Code and\n        Gemini instead of being written twice.\n\n-   Fixed generated `ptbk` prompt emoji tags so `coder add`, `coder generate-boilerplates`, refactor prompt generation, and `coder find-fresh-emoji-tags` share one Unicode-valid single-pictogram catalogue instead of a duplicated legacy list containing non-emoji symbols. The emoji-tag scan cache now records the candidate catalogue fingerprint and rescans when it changes, so an already assigned tag such as `[✨🛼]` is not mistaken for a fresh tag after an update.\n\n-   Added remaining subscription-limit visibility to the rich **ptbk coder** terminal dashboard.\n\n    -   The `Session` box now lists every rolling limit a selected harness reports, including its remaining percentage\n        and reset time. It does not assume a fixed pair of windows, so a 5-hour, weekly, model-specific, or future\n        additional limit all render as separate aligned rows.\n    -   OpenAI Codex reads its current account snapshot through the Codex app-server protocol, while Claude Code\n        reuses its normal `stream-json` rate-limit events instead of spending a separate quota-only prompt. Other\n        harnesses keep their existing behavior until they implement the same optional runner capability.\n    -   Updated the **ptbk coder** landing-page terminal demo and pacing copy to show the new 5-hour and 7-day\n        subscription rows.\n\n-   Let you decide what **ptbk coder** does with a dirty working tree. The clean-working-tree guard used to be a yes/no\n    question — either the coder refused to start, or `--ignore-git-changes` waved the changes through. The far more\n    common case had no answer at all: a run that was killed or crashed mid-task, leaving half-finished work in the tree\n    and one prompt stuck in the in-progress `[^]` status. The only way forward was to throw that work away.\n\n    -   **The new `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` replaces `--ignore-git-changes`**, which is gone; use\n        `--git-changes ignore` instead. `fail` stays the default and now says in its error which of the other two modes\n        to reach for.\n    -   **`--git-changes continue` resumes the interrupted prompt** with its uncommitted changes still in place. It\n        expects **exactly one** prompt in the `[^]` status and refuses to guess otherwise: finding none or finding\n        several fails with a message naming the prompts it found, because the changes in the tree cannot be attributed\n        to a single task. Only that one round runs on the dirty tree — once it is committed, every later round expects a\n        clean working tree again. It cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree is checked out from the\n        last commit and would leave exactly those changes behind, or `--test-before yes-and-fix`, which has no\n        unmodified project state to verify and repair.\n    -   **A prompt one harness started and another one finished says so in chronological order.** A resumed status\n        now reads `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high` - Implementation in progress ``,\n        and the `[x]` and `[!]` lines keep that report. Each further `--git-changes continue` invocation extends the\n        same report with another `interrupted, continued by …` segment, so no earlier harness is dropped; resuming the\n        same harness keeps its existing authentication label instead of naming it twice. The live status still reports\n        its active phase, but the final continuation report omits its partial step usage and duration rather than\n        presenting them as the whole task. All three statuses go through one\n        [`formatPromptRunnerAttribution`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/prompts/promptRunnerAttribution.ts), which also\n        understands the reverse-ordered `started by` status lines written by the preceding version.\n    -   `ptbk coder server` and `ptbk agent-folder run` share the same flag. An agent folder answers queued messages\n        instead of running a prompt queue, so `continue` keeps the changes there exactly like `ignore` does.\n\n-   Made the terminal controls of **ptbk coder** answer every key press. Pressing `P`, `S` or `X` used to be a leap of\n    faith: `S Skip current waiting` in particular changed nothing on screen, so there was no way to tell whether the key\n    had arrived, whether the wait was being skipped, or whether the terminal had simply stopped repainting.\n\n    -   **Every press is now answered inside the `Controls` box**, on the frame that follows it, for example\n        `» S Skipping the current waiting, continuing right now`. A press which changes nothing is answered too\n        (`» S Nothing to skip, the coder is not waiting right now`), because \"nothing happened\" and \"the key was lost\"\n        must not look the same. The answer fades after a few seconds and repeated identical answers are counted\n        (`(×2)`), so even pressing the same control twice redraws the frame.\n    -   **`S` now really skips the wait it is offered for.** The control is shown during every `waiting` phase, but two\n        of those waits were never registered as skippable and quietly ignored the key: the Claude Code session-limit\n        wait before a `--resume` resurrection, which can hold a run for hours, and the `ptbk coder server` keep-alive\n        poll. Both go through\n        [`waitForSkippableWorldTimeDeadline`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/waitForSkippableWorldTimeDeadline.ts)\n        now, the single way the coder waits for a deadline the user may cut short, which\n        [`sleepWithCountdown`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/sleepWithCountdown.ts) already used for the pacing\n        and error waits.\n    -   **The keys are handled in exactly one place.** The rich terminal UI and the plain `--no-ui` console listener\n        each had their own copy of the `P`/`S`/`X` dispatch, and only the plain one said anything back.\n        [`applyCoderRunControlKey`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/applyCoderRunControlKey.ts) performs the action\n        and describes it, and both front ends render that one description through\n        [`formatCoderRunControlFeedback`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/common/formatCoderRunControlFeedback.ts). The\n        `ptbk agent-folder run` dashboard, which shares the same renderer, answers its controls the same way.\n\n-   Took the ASCII `PTBK.IO` wordmark out of the **ptbk coder** terminal dashboard. The area above the `Session` box now\n    stays empty until the `--agent` avatar has been rendered, instead of being filled with a block-character logo that\n    was only ever a placeholder. It flashed at every start-up, and it stayed on screen for the whole run whenever no\n    agent was selected or its avatar could not be rasterized.\n\n    -   The header is still decided in one place,\n        [`buildFrameHeaderVisual`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/ui/buildCoderRunUiFrame.ts): it draws the agent avatar\n        as soon as [`buildCoderRunAgentVisual`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/ui/buildCoderRunAgentVisual.ts) hands one\n        over, and draws nothing before that.\n    -   `buildCoderRunOctopusVisual.ts`, which existed only to paint that wordmark, is gone.\n\n-   Simplified the comparison table on the **ptbk coder** landing page. Fifteen rows became nine, and the three agent\n    columns stopped repeating themselves: where Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and opencode make the same claim, the table\n    draws one cell across all three instead of printing the same sentence side by side three times. Exactly one row\n    still splits them, the one about moving your agent to another vendor, and that is the row worth stopping at.\n\n    -   **The rows that carried no signal are gone.** \"Human in the loop\" was a check mark in all four columns, which\n        tells a visitor nothing, and the features section explains it anyway. Thin slices of one idea were merged:\n        tests before the first task and tests after every task are one row now, and the three separate git rows\n        (commit identity, pull and push, worktree per task) are one.\n    -   **The support levels mean something again.** The matrix already ruled that anything you can script yourself is\n        `do-it-yourself` and never `not-available`, yet pacing and pre-flight tests were marked `not-available`.\n        `not-available` now means the tool has no such concept, such as a queue or a backlog, while `do-it-yourself`\n        means it hands you the pieces, such as a hook or a session to ask in.\n    -   Every claim about a compared harness is written once in the data instead of three times, so the two products\n        that genuinely differ cannot drift apart by a typo. Notes of `ptbk coder` cells are now the flag or command\n        itself, which is what makes them render in monospace, and a long one like `--wait-between-prompts` breaks\n        inside the word instead of spilling into the neighbouring column.\n\n-   Rewrote the copy of the **ptbk coder** landing page so it reads like a developer wrote it. Not one em dash is left\n    in the visible text, and neither are the phrases that gave the page away: \"an autonomous, versioned development\n    loop\", \"everything around the agent is handled by ptbk coder\", \"part of the Promptbook ecosystem\". Passive\n    sentences now name who does the work, the long ones are split in two, and adverbs propping up weak verbs are gone.\n\n    -   **One benefit card was saying the opposite of what it meant.** \"Revert that commit and both the implementation\n        and its done state return together\" described a revert as bringing work back. It now reads \"Revert the commit\n        and the checkbox goes back to `[ ]` together with the code.\"\n    -   **The `<title>` separator is a colon instead of an em dash**, so the browser tab and the Google result read\n        `ptbk coder: Your coding agents, running your backlog`. The search description and the sharing description were\n        rewritten as well, both still short enough for the lengths the build validates.\n    -   The hero no longer promises work \"even while you sleep\" and the features lead no longer hides behind \"is\n        handled by\". Both now say which commands run and which keys stop them.\n    -   The specs under [`apps/coder-landing/specs/`](../apps/coder-landing/specs/) quote the page copy verbatim, so\n        every rewritten sentence was updated there in the same pass and the page stays re-implementable from its specs\n        alone.\n\n-   Gave the **ptbk coder** landing page the metadata it deserves when it is shared or found. Everything it says about\n    itself — titles, descriptions, URLs, keywords and the publisher — now comes from one module, so the page, its\n    sharing preview, its structured data and its sitemap can never contradict each other.\n\n    -   **A sharing preview instead of a blank rectangle.** The page declared a `summary_large_image` card without ever\n        offering an image, so every link to it arrived on LinkedIn, Discord or Slack as a bare headline. Both the Open\n        Graph and the Twitter image are now generated from the page data itself: the brand logo and the domain, the\n        two-line tagline, the sharing description, and a terminal window showing the very install and run commands the\n        quickstart teaches. Because it is built from the same data modules as the page, it cannot go stale.\n    -   **Everything Google looks for.** A canonical link, `robots` and `googlebot` directives with large image\n        previews and unlimited snippets, the publisher and author, the locale, the theme color, the Apple touch icon —\n        and a `metadataBase`, so every metadata URL resolves absolutely. Titles and descriptions are checked against\n        the length at which search engines truncate them, so copy that would be cut off fails the build instead of the\n        preview.\n    -   **The page now explains itself in JSON-LD.** One structured-data graph tells search engines about the company\n        behind the page, the website, the page itself and `ptbk coder` as a `SoftwareApplication` — with its operating\n        systems, requirements, repository, license and feature list. The features and the supported harnesses are read\n        from the same data modules the page renders, so the structured data can never claim a feature a visitor cannot\n        see.\n    -   **Added `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`**, both built from the canonical URL. The sitemap lists the single route\n        of the page, because its sections are anchors inside it rather than pages of their own.\n    -   The new [`specs/metadata.md`](../apps/coder-landing/specs/metadata.md) documents all of it, so the page keeps\n        being re-implementable from its specs alone.\n\n-   Fixed horizontal overflow on the **ptbk coder** landing page on mobile. The accessible labels of comparison-table\n    support marks now remain within their icons, and responsive feature and harness cards can shrink to the viewport\n    instead of creating an empty scrollable area at the right edge.\n\n-   Redesigned the **ptbk coder** landing page benefits around unattended PRD runs, portable `.book` agents, and PRD/code state that travels together in git commits. The visual cards now use centered code-native illustrations, and the comparison table brings those three advantages to the top.\n\n-   Fixed cyclic Agents Server `FROM` inheritance so resolution stops at the cycle edge as if it used `FROM @Null`.\n    Pages and APIs now continue to resolve while the existing Book editor warning identifies the cycle for repair.\n\n-   Fixed the Book editor `PERSONA` deprecation diagnostic regression test to assert the replacement guidance defined in the shared commitment catalog.\n\n-   Deprecated `PERSONA` for newly created Agents Server books. New-agent boilerplates and onboarding templates now use `GOAL` and `RULE` commitments, while the Book editor yellow-underlines every commitment marked as deprecated in the shared catalog and explains its replacement.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server's effective `FROM` inheritance handling. An explicitly selected parent now fully replaces\n    implicit Adam inheritance, while that parent's own chain is still materialized normally; only the final `FROM`\n    participates in both runtime resolution and missing-reference diagnostics. The Book editor now warns directly on\n    local inheritance cycles and when the core Adam agent does not explicitly inherit from `@Null`/`@Void`.\n\n-   Made **`@Adam` the implicit ancestor of every agent**, so a book that says nothing about inheritance behaves\n    exactly like one writing `FROM @Adam` or `FROM {Adam}`. An agent that should start from nothing says so explicitly\n    with `FROM @Null` (or `FROM {Void}`), and the Book language manual now documents both halves of that rule.\n\n    -   **A missing Adam stopped being silent.** Because the ancestor is implicit, a server whose core `Adam` agent had\n        been deleted inherited nothing without ever saying so. The Book editor now shows the very same \"referenced\n        agent was not found\" card on its right panel as if the book had written `FROM {Adam}` itself — right away,\n        without the author having to write the reference first to discover the problem. Whether a core agent is there\n        is read from the same status the Core Agents page renders, so the card and the page it links to can never\n        disagree, and a namesake on a federated server never hides an ancestor this server cannot actually load.\n    -   **The card offers the repair, not just the complaint.** A core agent is bundled with the server, so instead of\n        the ordinary \"create it from scratch\" button the card reinstates it from its repository book, names every other\n        core agent missing at the same time — one click brings back all of them — and links to the Core Agents admin\n        page. Reinstating is offered only to administrators, runs through the same reinstate flow the home page notice\n        and the Core Agents page already use, and refreshes the panel once the agents are back.\n    -   The same recovery is attached to an explicitly written reference, so `FROM {Adam}` on a server without Adam\n        offers to reinstate the core agent instead of creating an empty one that would shadow it.\n    -   **A book that declares its parent twice no longer breaks.** An agent has exactly one parent, so a repeated\n        `FROM` used to abort the whole resolution with an error. The last `FROM` now simply wins and overrides every\n        earlier one, which are dropped from the resolved source instead of being loaded, and the Book editor warns on\n        every `FROM` keyword involved — telling the overridden ones which line took their place.\n    -   Implicit inheritance recognizes the current agent's URL aliases as well as its canonical URL, preventing the\n        Adam core agent from resolving as its own parent when it is addressed by a name URL but stored under a\n        permanent-ID URL.\n    -   **A reinstated Adam is found again.** The implicit ancestor is addressed by the well-known name `adam`, and an\n        agent name used to resolve to the oldest agent that ever carried it — including one sitting in the recycle bin.\n        On a server where the core `Adam` had been deleted and reinstated, the name therefore pointed at the deleted\n        leftover, its source could no longer be loaded, and every book without `FROM` quietly inherited nothing while\n        an explicitly written `FROM @Adam` kept working, because that path resolves through the list of agents that\n        exist. An agent that exists now always wins over a deleted namesake, so both halves of the rule agree again. A\n        deleted agent stays resolvable when no live agent answers to that name, which is how the recycle bin restores\n        one.\n\n-   Added a **planned-message manager** to the Agents Server, so an administrator can finally see and steer every\n    timeout every agent planned — not only the one agent whose goal chat happens to be open. It lives in the same tab\n    group as the task manager, because the task manager answers \"what is running right now\" while this answers \"what\n    keeps making it run\".\n\n    -   **The whole life of a plan, in one place.** Planned messages are listed with the wake-ups still ahead, the ones\n        whose starting date has not arrived yet, the ones waking an agent right now, the ones being held back, and the\n        ones that are over — whether they were cancelled, ran out of runs, or passed their ending date. A finished plan\n        keeps its row and says which of those three ended it, so the manager also answers what a planned message did\n        before it stopped.\n    -   **Steering, not just watching.** Any planned message of any agent can be re-planned, held back and let go\n        again, or cancelled. Re-planning goes through the very same planned-message service an agent re-plans itself\n        with, so an administrator can never write a schedule the agent itself could not have written, and a planned\n        message that is firing at that very moment says so instead of quietly losing the change.\n    -   **Filters made of the plan itself.** The listing narrows by stage, by agent, by how often a message repeats\n        (a fixed interval, a cron, or a single wake-up), by when it last woke its agent, and by free text over the\n        message, its agent, its chat, and its owner. Every row links straight to the agent that planned it and to the\n        chat it wakes.\n\n-   Turned Agents Server planned messages from \"repeats every N milliseconds until cancelled\" into a real schedule, so\n    an agent can plan a message that repeats, one that runs exactly once, and anything between the two. Each planned\n    message can now carry a **cron expression**, a **total number of runs**, and a **starting and ending date**, and it\n    finishes by itself once that schedule is over.\n\n    -   **One schedule, one place deciding it.** A planned message follows either a fixed interval or a five-field cron\n        expression, bounded by `startsAt`, `endsAt`, and `maxRunCount`. A single resolver answers when the message wakes\n        the agent first, when it wakes it again, and when the plan is over, so scheduling, repeating, and finishing can\n        never disagree. The cron engine is the one already used by the automatic VPS self-update, which was extracted\n        into a shared utility instead of being written a second time.\n    -   **A finished plan disappears.** A message that ran as many times as it was planned to run, or whose ending date\n        passed, becomes terminal instead of being re-armed, and a wake-up delayed past its own ending date is dropped\n        rather than fired late. Finished messages are therefore never listed to the agent, never sent into its prompt,\n        and never wake it again — the agent only ever sees what is still ahead.\n    -   **The agent can re-plan, not only plan and cancel.** A new `update` action changes the schedule or the text of a\n        planned message while keeping its identifier, so a wake-up an agent already announced stays the same wake-up.\n        Only the named fields change, and `null` removes a bound.\n    -   **From every invocation.** Planning, re-planning, and cancelling work the same way from a normal chat, from an\n        external chat such as an email or API conversation, from a goal chat woken by a planned message itself, and from\n        the goal-chat turn queued when the agent's book was updated — all of them go through the one shared\n        planned-message service, reached through the planned-message sidecar of the answering runner, the model tools,\n        or the internal runtime API.\n    -   The goal chat lists the cron, the run counter, and the date window next to the repeat interval it showed before,\n        and the wake-up message itself now says which run of the plan it is.\n\n-   Made every Agents Server agent project a git repository whose history is written by the agent itself, and turned\n    the popup behind a **📁 project** chip into a card that is actually worth opening. Clicking the chip used to show\n    little more than the project directory name; it now shows what the project is, what state it is in, and the exact\n    diff of what that very message did to it.\n\n    -   **Every project is a git repository.** The local agent runner initializes one for a project which is not a\n        repository yet and commits everything an answer changed into it, under the same message as the answered\n        message itself. Agents are told about this in their projects prompt section, so nothing has to `git init` or\n        commit by hand anymore, and work done in a project stays recoverable and reviewable as normal history. A\n        project which already belongs to a repository around the agent folder is deliberately left to that\n        repository instead of being turned into an embedded one, and a freshly initialized repository gets ignore\n        rules so installed dependencies and `.env` secrets never enter an automatic commit.\n    -   **The card shows the project.** Its running state and status label, a link opening the running project in a\n        new tab, a link opening its project page in a new tab, plus its size, file count and whether it is a git\n        repository — all resolved through the same helpers the project page itself uses, so the chip and the page it\n        links to can never describe one project differently.\n    -   **The card shows the change.** How many files the message changed with the added and removed line counts, the\n        commit it created, the list of changed files, and the unified diff itself with added, removed and context\n        lines told apart. A change too large to carry into a chat is shortened and says so.\n    -   A project the answer committed something into now gets a chip even when nothing in the harness log named it,\n        because a project that was changed was obviously worked with.\n\n-   Added Agents Server chips below a chat answer for every source outside the agent it touched, so an answer never\n    silently reaches beyond the agent again. An agent that reviews a Gmail mailbox and drafts a mail now says so with\n    a **🔌 Gmail** chip below its message, exactly like the project and wake-up chips already added next to the source\n    chips that show the knowledge behind an answer.\n\n    This completes the same universal pattern rather than adding a second one: the local agent runner resolves what\n    the answering coding harness really reached from its live runtime log — which is deleted the moment a message is\n    answered — reports it in the run-report sidecar it already writes, and the server turns each source into one chip\n    on the assistant message. The chips therefore show up in normal chats, in the goal chat, and when an external\n    chat such as an email conversation is opened, while the outbound email itself is still rendered from the answer\n    text alone and stays unchanged.\n\n    -   **Integrations** such as Gmail or Google Calendar are recognized from the integration tool calls of both\n        supported harnesses and shown under their human-readable name.\n    -   **Websites** are shown by hostname, both when the harness fetched an address directly and when it ran a\n        network client such as `curl` or `wget` in the shell.\n    -   **Web searches** are shown with the query that was looked up.\n    -   Work an agent does only inside itself still produces no chip at all. Only harness tool payloads are\n        inspected, so an address or service merely mentioned in the conversation — or written into a file the agent\n        edits — is never reported as touched, and addresses of the machine the agent runs on are dropped because they\n        are internal.\n\n-   Added `--period <duration>` to `ptbk coder ping`. Without it the ping stays exactly what it was — one tiny dummy\n    prompt, one reported result, done. With it that very same ping repeats once per period until it is stopped with\n    `CTRL+C`, which keeps the quota window of a harness permanently refreshing for a handful of tokens per ping.\n    Pinging `claude-code` with `--period 5h` therefore keeps the **Claude Code 5-hour limit window always open**, so a\n    queue started at any hour already has a fresh window waiting instead of burning the first minutes of it.\n\n    -   The period is measured from the start of one ping to the start of the next one, so `--period 5h` really pings\n        every 5 hours instead of every 5 hours plus however long a ping happens to take. It is a wall-clock deadline,\n        so a computer which falls asleep during a period does not stretch it.\n    -   A ping which fails is reported and the loop simply continues with the next period, because a keep-alive which\n        dies on the first hiccup is not a keep-alive.\n    -   The duration uses the same `5h`, `30m`, `1h30m` format as the `--wait-*` options of `ptbk coder run` and is\n        rejected when it is not a positive one, so `--period` can never become a loop without a pause between rounds.\n    -   The `ptbk coder` landing page presents this as an advanced feature of its own.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server planned-message chips hiding the numeric part of their scheduled time. The chip now uses the\n    shared chat typography for its text while retaining the existing OpenMoji fallback for its stopwatch icon, so a\n    label such as **“Timeout: 10:28 AM”** renders exactly as it is copied.\n\n-   Fixed misleading **Goal Chat** response timing. The old label measured from the time a message entered the local\n    runner queue, so a scheduled wake-up could claim it took many hours to answer even when the agent had only just\n    run. The coding harness now records its real start and finish times in the existing answer report; the server uses\n    those timestamps for the completed answer's time and duration. Goal Chat now says **“executed for …”**, while an\n    older runner report with no execution timing shows no misleading queue-age duration.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server goal-chat planned messages from `setTimeout` to `setInterval`. A planned message used to be\n    consumed by its own firing, so an agent whose goal is \"check emails every 5 minutes\" had to re-plan the very same\n    wake-up on every single invocation — and the moment one answer forgot to, the goal chat was left with **No planned\n    messages** and the agent never woke up again.\n\n    A planned message now repeats at the interval it was planned with until it is cancelled, which makes **keeping the\n    current plan the default**: an invoked agent sees its planned messages with their intervals and does nothing at all\n    while they still match its goal. When the goal changes to \"every 10 minutes\", the agent cancels the message that no\n    longer matches and sets one with the interval its goal now requires.\n\n    -   The durable timeout of a repeating message is re-armed in place after each firing instead of scheduling a\n        successor row, so one plan keeps one `timeoutId` for its whole life. The identifier an agent saw while it was\n        answering therefore still cancels the message when its answer is applied minutes later, and a crash between two\n        repetitions can never leave two schedules behind.\n    -   The wake-up turn of each repetition stays idempotent by carrying how many times its timeout already fired.\n    -   The planned-message sidecar, the runtime tools, the goal-chat notes, and the planned-message panel of the goal\n        chat all show the repeat interval, so an agent (and a person) can compare the plan with the goal instead of\n        guessing from a single due time.\n    -   An interval shorter than one minute is rejected, because a repeating message with a tiny interval would be an\n        unattended self-invocation loop rather than a plan.\n\n-   Fixed an Agents Server agent referencing a project it just created as a plain link, which turned into a proper\n    project chip only after the page was reloaded.
